name: finalize_audit

quality.summary: Code quality is uneven. The newer action classes are well-structured and use strict types throughout, but there are notable issues: duplicate API-key checks, debug comments left in production code (CompletionAction), a non-functional `require-dev` key in composer.json, and two identical Python scripts. The SuggestSolutionsAction duplicates prompt logic already present in AIServicePromptBuilder.

findings.title: Duplicate API-key guard in GeneratePredictionDraftsAction
findings.description: Lines 43-46 and 48-51 perform identical checks (`config('openai.api_key')` empty-string guard) back to back. This is dead, confusing code that suggests a copy-paste mistake.
findings.fix: Remove the second identical block (lines 48-51). One guard is sufficient.

findings.title: require-dev block in composer.json uses wrong key and is inert
findings.description: The dev dependencies are listed under `require-dev_comment` instead of `require-dev`. This means tools like phpstan, psalm, rector, pint, and phpinsights are never actually installed as Composer dev dependencies, giving a false impression of quality tooling.
findings.fix: Rename the key to `require-dev` and verify each tool installs correctly.

findings.title: Production debug output left as comment in CompletionAction
findings.description: Lines 44-64 of CompletionAction.php contain a large comment block with raw OpenAI API debug output, including token counts and internal response object dumps. This is dead code that adds noise and could confuse future maintainers.
findings.snippet:
/*
The model `text-davinci-003` has been deprecated...
+text: " a recursive acronym for..."
...
*/
findings.fix: Remove the comment block entirely. Any useful notes should go in the changelog or docs.

findings.title: Duplicated Python fine-tuning script (bin/ vs scripts/)
findings.description: bin/fine_tuning.py and scripts/fine_tuning.py are byte-for-byte identical (4523 bytes each). Likewise test_fine_tuning.py is duplicated. Maintaining two copies guarantees they will diverge.
findings.fix: Delete one copy and add a symlink, or move the canonical version to a shared location with a single entry point.

findings.title: Prompt logic duplicated between SuggestSolutionsAction and AIServicePromptBuilder
findings.description: The solutions prompt template in SuggestSolutionsAction::buildSolutionPrompt() (lines 56-79) is nearly identical to AIServicePromptBuilder::solutions(). Two sources of truth for the same prompt will diverge silently.
findings.snippet: private function buildSolutionPrompt(...): string { return "Suggerisci soluzioni..."; }
findings.fix: Delete buildSolutionPrompt() and delegate to AIServicePromptBuilder::solutions().

performance.summary: The retry back-off in AIChatCompletionClient uses a blocking sleep() call which blocks the PHP worker process entirely. Cache keys for AIService methods use md5 over unbounded input arrays, which is fine for correctness but the serialization of large ticket/agent arrays on every cache miss is wasteful. No rate-limiting is enforced for the OpenAI calls made from GeneratePredictionDraftsAction.

findings.title: Blocking sleep() in retry loop stalls PHP worker
findings.description: AIChatCompletionClient::request() calls `sleep(pow(2, $attempt))` (up to 8 seconds for 3 attempts) inside a synchronous while loop. This ties up a PHP-FPM worker for the full sleep duration, reducing server concurrency under load. With retryAttempts=3, a worst-case request can block a worker for 2+4+8=14 seconds.
findings.fix: Dispatch retries as queued jobs using spatie/queueable-action (already a dependency) instead of sleeping inline. If synchronous retry is required, use usleep() with a shorter initial delay and add jitter.

findings.title: Hardcoded gpt-4 model in AIChatCompletionClient ignores config
findings.description: AIChatCompletionClient::attemptChatCompletion() hardcodes `'model' => 'gpt-4'` (line 59) rather than reading from config. gpt-4 is significantly more expensive and slower than gpt-4o-mini or gpt-3.5-turbo. The config system (ai.chat_model) is bypassed entirely for this client.
findings.fix: Read the model from config: `'model' => config('ai.chat_model', 'gpt-4o-mini')`.

architecture.summary: The module mixes two distinct domains (FixCity ticket management and prediction markets) in the same service layer without clear boundaries. There is no HTTP controller layer for the AI API routes (the entire routes/api.php is commented out), yet the action classes exist. Config key inconsistency across three different namespaces (services.openai.*, openai.*, ai.*) signals the module evolved without a unifying contract.

findings.title: All API routes are commented out — module has no live HTTP surface
findings.description: routes/api.php contains a full set of REST routes wrapped in a block comment. The AIController class referenced does not appear to exist. This means the module provides no functional HTTP API despite declaring one, and all entry points are through internal action classes only.
findings.fix: Either implement AIController and uncomment the routes, or remove the commented block to avoid misleading documentation.

findings.title: Three inconsistent config namespaces for OpenAI configuration
findings.description: API key and model config are read from `services.openai.*`, `openai.*`, and `ai.*` in different files with no single canonical source. This makes it impossible to configure the module from one place and causes silent misconfigurations.
findings.fix: Centralise all OpenAI config reads in a single AIConfig value object or in config/ai.php, then inject it via the service container.

findings.title: AIServiceJsonDecoder and AiJsonResponseDecoder are near-identical duplicate classes
findings.description: Modules\AI\Services\AIServiceJsonDecoder and Modules\AI\Support\AiJsonResponseDecoder implement virtually the same JSON decoding logic (trim, json_decode, string-key filter, return [] on error). Having two classes for the same responsibility causes divergence.
findings.snippet:
class AiJsonResponseDecoder { public static function decodeObject(string $result): array {...} }
// mirrors AIServiceJsonDecoder::decodeObject()
findings.fix: Delete one class and update all call sites to use the canonical implementation.

findings.title: AIService instantiates AIChatCompletionClient directly in constructor
findings.description: AIService::__construct() manually constructs AIChatCompletionClient with `new AIChatCompletionClient(...)`, bypassing the service container. This makes the client impossible to mock in tests without reflection and couples the service to a concrete implementation.
findings.fix: Bind AIChatCompletionClient in the service provider and inject it via constructor injection: `public function __construct(private readonly AIChatCompletionClient $client) {}`.

testing.summary: The module has test infrastructure and some well-structured Pest tests for GeneratePredictionsAction and CompletionAction, but critical paths have skipped tests, the audit-coverage directory contains 16 trivially fake bridge tests (assertTrue(true)) that inflate file counts without providing real coverage, and GeneratePredictionDraftsAction has only one real test scenario.

findings.title: 16 audit bridge tests are permanently trivial (assertTrue(true))
findings.description: The entire audit-coverage/tests/ directory contains 16 files (01 through 16) each containing a single test: `self::assertTrue(true)`. These are not executed in CI (the file comment says so) and provide zero coverage. They inflate the test file count and may fool superficial tooling.
findings.fix: Delete the audit-coverage directory entirely, or replace the placeholder tests with real smoke tests for the module's key integration points.

findings.title: Critical test cases explicitly skipped with markTestSkipped
findings.description: Three tests in GeneratePredictionsActionTest are permanently skipped: 'uses fallback when OpenAI API key is not configured', 'handles empty topic gracefully', and 'respects rate limiting in batch generation'. These cover real failure modes and edge cases.
findings.fix: Implement the skipped tests. Config manipulation is trivially achievable with `config()->set()` as shown in GeneratePredictionDraftsActionTest line 15.

findings.title: AIService and AIChatCompletionClient have no unit tests
findings.description: The core service layer (AIService, AIChatCompletionClient, AIServicePromptBuilder) has no dedicated tests. tests/Unit/Services/AIServiceTest.php exists but is only 542 bytes — likely empty or trivial.
findings.snippet: // 542 bytes — no meaningful test coverage for AIService
findings.fix: Add tests for each AIService public method using Http::fake() to simulate OpenAI responses, and verify cache key generation and JSON decoding behaviour.

findings.title: No test framework declared despite using Pest
findings.description: The project summary reports 'Test frameworks: none' even though Pest is actively used throughout the test suite. Pest is not listed in any dependency manifest (composer.json require-dev is broken due to QUAL-002), so it may only be available from the parent Laravel app's vendor.
findings.fix: Add `pestphp/pest` and `pestphp/pest-plugin-laravel` to a correctly-named `require-dev` block in composer.json.

documentation.summary: The docs/ folder is reasonably populated with workflow and practice guides. However there are two duplicate index files (docs/00-INDEX.md and docs/00-index.md differ only in case), the README is mostly marketing copy without setup instructions, and the entirely commented-out API surface is not documented anywhere.

findings.title: Duplicate doc index files differing only by filename case
findings.description: Both docs/00-INDEX.md and docs/00-index.md exist with identical content (33 lines each). On case-insensitive file systems (macOS, Windows) one will silently shadow the other; on Linux both exist creating maintenance confusion.
findings.fix: Delete docs/00-index.md and standardise on the uppercase variant (or vice versa).

findings.title: README provides no installation or configuration instructions
findings.description: The README.md contains marketing badges and a brief feature list but no instructions for installing the module, configuring the OpenAI API key, or running fine-tuning. Given the three inconsistent config namespaces discovered in the code, this omission makes onboarding very difficult.
findings.snippet:
## Superpoteri
- Connettori servizi AI
...
(no installation steps, no config keys documented)
findings.fix: Add an 'Installation & Configuration' section documenting the required env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, which config namespace to use) and how to run the Flask fine-tuning sidecar.

findings.title: Commented-out API routes create misleading documentation
findings.description: routes/api.php declares 9 REST endpoints in a comment block, implying they exist. No controller implements them. Any developer reading the routes file will assume the API is functional.
findings.fix: Either implement the controller and activate the routes, or remove the comment and document planned endpoints in a separate API design doc.

dependencies.summary: The only declared PHP dependency is `openai-php/laravel: *` with an unbounded version constraint, which is a significant risk. All dev tooling (phpstan, rector, pint, psalm) is listed under a malformed `require-dev_comment` key and is therefore never installed. The npm dependencies are reasonable but include axios as a dev dependency despite it being a runtime HTTP client in browser contexts.

findings.title: openai-php/laravel pinned to wildcard `*` version
findings.description: composer.json declares `"openai-php/laravel": "*"` with no version constraint. This allows Composer to install any major version, including breaking ones. A `composer update` could silently upgrade to a version with breaking API changes.
findings.fix: Pin to a specific compatible range, e.g. `"openai-php/laravel": "^0.10"`. Run `composer show openai-php/laravel` to identify the current installed version.

findings.title: Dev dependencies declared under invalid key — never installed
findings.description: All quality tooling (phpstan, larastan, psalm, rector, pint, phpinsights, enlightn) is under `require-dev_comment` — a non-standard key Composer ignores. This means the project's claimed PHPStan Level 10 and static analysis cannot actually run from this module's own composer.json.
findings.fix: Rename the key to `require-dev`. Verify each tool's version constraint is still compatible.

findings.title: Python fine-tuning service has no dependency manifest
findings.description: bin/fine_tuning.py imports flask, transformers, pandas, and torch but there is no requirements.txt or pyproject.toml. Anyone deploying the Flask sidecar has no reproducible way to install the correct versions, and there is no pinning against known-vulnerable versions of these libraries.
findings.snippet:
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, Trainer, TrainingArguments
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import torch, pandas as pd
findings.fix: Create a requirements.txt (or pyproject.toml) pinning flask, transformers, torch, and pandas to specific versions. Add it to the module root.

findings.title: dotenv / dotenv-expand versions are outdated in npm
findings.description: package.json lists `dotenv@^10.0.0` and `dotenv-expand@^5.1.0`. Current stable versions are dotenv@16+ and dotenv-expand@11+. These older versions may miss bug fixes relevant to environment variable handling.
findings.fix: Update to `dotenv@^16` and `dotenv-expand@^11`. Run `npm audit` after updating to check for known CVEs.

outputPreview: Audit finalized. Thank you.
